doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jarmo Savolainen's True Image and Dave Panichi's date
summary: They recall Finnish pianist Jarmo Savolainen from IASJ meetings and his sad death, and a Dave Panichi album.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I’ve heard many good things along those lines about him. Here’s a date from ’94 with the late, lamented Jarmo Savolainen.
Great record. We did it for Finnish radio.
With Jukkis, right? And Anders Jormin.
No, this is with Tim Hagens, Sonny Heinila, a Finnish tenor player, Jarmo on piano, of course, and Ron McClure and Billy Hart.
I don’t remember that. I’m thinking of another one.
This is done in Brooklyn for A Records.
A Records. Yep, it’s Jarmo’s date. Jarmo is very – came to all the IASJ meetings.
That’s where I met him. I actually played with him and Jukkis. I did a week in Helsinki in 2002. I was very saddened to hear.
Great guy. Yeah, it was devastating, tragic.
I guess they just found him on the street.
We were speaking earlier about Dave Panichi. Here he is.
That’s the record. What’s the date on that? The [?Go For].
This is with – you’re on one track. Rich Perry’s on the rest, along with Mulgrew Miller, Jay Anderson, and Victor Lewis.
I have it confused with another thing, but I guess that’s the date.
